newsitem.title: UK: European VGO quiet but stronger with U.S. demandS.
newsitem.headline: European VGO quiet but stronger with U.S. demandS.

text.p: European vacuum gas oil ended the week firmer with traders saying buying interest was coming in from the United States and recent trans-Atlantic shipments will firm barge prices soon.
No fresh deals were heard but traders said the buy/sell range for low sulphur VGO cargoes in Northwest Europe rose to about $115/$118 from $113/$117 in mid-week.
The net back from selling the material in the United States was around $117/$118, they added.
"There's more demand and not very much (supplies) around and traders are still looking to take to the Gulf Coast...So it is tightening," one trader said.
A refiner who sells low-sulphur VGO said that demand from mainland Europe was not that high though "just bits and pieces in the barges market."
A low-sulphur VGO barge seller said that with low sulphur going trans-Atlantic recently, "We are in a position to increase prices."
He said his levels were about $121/$123 for low sulphur barges, and should increase soon with local demand for July strong, adding that high sulphur VGO barges were roughly $10 a tonne lower.
"No one is really interested in high sulphur, though everyone is looking at low sulphur," the trader said, adding he expected to strike a few deals early next week.
